deep.reconstruction:
Context (cote 151, 'Topos stratifié'): a stratified space or topos X is indexed by a poset I of strata X_i^*. For a pair i<j there is a 'fundamental diagram', referred to as (17)/(19) on the previous page:
  X_i^* → V_{i,j} ← V_{i,j}^* → X_j^*.
Here V_{i,j} is a (tubular) neighbourhood of X_i^* in the closure part X_{i}∪X_{j}, and X_i^* → V_{i,j} is a homotopy equivalence. V_{i,j}^* = V_{i,j} − X_i^* is the deleted neighbourhood (the 'link' or boundary of the tube), which lies in, and maps to, the open stratum X_j^*. Up to homotopy this is the span X_i ← holink(X_i,X_j) → X_j of Quinn / exit-path theory.

On the previous page Grothendieck turns the poset I into an auxiliary diagram (a small category) Ĩ:
- vertices: i^* (one per element), and [i,j], [i,j]^* (two per elementary interval, i.e. j a successor of i);
- arrows: [i,j]^* → [i,j] ← i^* and [i,j]^* → j^* (three per elementary interval).
So #vertices = card I + 2ν and #arrows = 3ν, where ν is the number of elementary intervals. A stratified object then gives a functor Ĩ → (spaces/topoi): i^* ↦ X_i^*, [i,j] ↦ V_{i,j}, [i,j]^* ↦ V_{i,j}^*.

This page draws Ĩ in examples.
- (20) I = Δ_n gives a staircase zigzag X_0^* → V_{01} ← V_{01}^* → X_1^* → V_{12} ← V_{12}^* → X_2^* → … → X_n^*, with 3n arrows.
- (21) I = {0→a, 0→b} (a common minimum below two maximal elements) gives V_{0b}^*→V_{0b}←X_0^*→V_{0a}←V_{0a}^*, with V_{0a}^*→X_a^* and V_{0b}^*→X_b^*.
- (22) I = {a→c←b} gives X_a^*→V_{ac}←V_{ac}^*→X_c^*←V_{bc}^*→V_{bc}←X_b^*.

The page then starts the next step, continued on the next page: suppose I carries a 'dimension function' d: I→Z such that, for i≤j, d(j)=d(i)+1 iff j is a successor of i. Then one can take disjoint unions by dimension, X_m^* = ⊔_{d(i)=m} X_i^*, etc. This collapses Ĩ to the linear staircase (20) indexed by dimension, with some vertices possibly empty.

Purpose: to give a combinatorial 'dévissage' model of a stratified space or topos by its strata and tubular-neighbourhood/link data. This is the kind of equivalence 'stratified structure ↔ gluing data of strata and tube boundaries' that Grothendieck advertises in Esquisse d'un programme §5.
errors: Ĩ only records links for elementary intervals (j a successor of i). For posets of depth ≥2, e.g. Δ_n with n≥2, the homotopy type of a stratified space also needs links for non-adjacent pairs (X_0 to X_2) and the coherences between them; modern treatments use functors on the subdivision sd(I), i.e. all chains. As drawn, the diagrams (20)–(22) are only a truncation of the full data. Possibly Grothendieck intends extra structure on V_{i,j} to carry the rest; this is not stated here.

In (22) the vertical arrow between V_{a,c} and V_{a,c}^* is drawn as a thick double-headed arrow. By the general pattern (19), and by the parallel V_{b,c} ← V_{b,c}^* on the same diagram, it should be the single arrow V_{a,c}^* → V_{a,c}.
Minor: in (21) the notation 0 for the minimal element • is introduced silently.

ideas.what: Encoding a two-stratum stratified space by the span stratum ← (tube ⊃ deleted tube) → open stratum, i.e. X_i^* → V_ij ← V_ij^* → X_j^*
ideas.modern_name: homotopy link / holink gluing data; recollement of a stratified space
ideas.usually_credited_to: Quinn (homotopically stratified sets, 1988); earlier Thom–Mather control data; Siebenmann
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5 (dévissage of stratified structures via tubular neighbourhoods), stated informally

ideas.what: Auxiliary category Ĩ built from the stratification poset I (vertices i*, [i,j], [i,j]* over elementary intervals; 3ν arrows), with a stratified object as a functor Ĩ → spaces/topoi
ideas.modern_name: diagram of links indexed by a subdivision-type category (cf. functors on sd(P) in exit-path / decomposition theorems)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Lurie (Higher Algebra, exit paths); Haine, Douteau, Barwick–Glasman–Haine (2018–2020)

ideas.what: Collapsing strata by a dimension function d satisfying d(j)=d(i)+1 iff j is a successor of i, to obtain one linear staircase indexed by Z
ideas.modern_name: grading of a stratification by dimension; ranked poset

missed.claim: Grothendieck sketches a combinatorial indexing category Ĩ for the 'dévissage' of a stratified topos by strata and tube/link data, worked out on examples (Δ_n, a two-branch V, a cospan). This is an early, explicit form of the later 'stratified space = diagram of links over a poset-derived category' philosophy. It is restricted to elementary intervals, and the higher coherence data is left open.
missed.quote: Avec l'ens ordonné I, fabriquons ... un diagramme dont les sommets sont des symboles i*, [i,j], [i,j]*, où i,j∈I, j successeur de i
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mainly historical: it anticipates the decomposition theorems for stratified homotopy types (Haine, Douteau, Barwick–Glasman–Haine). It also raises the question of when elementary-interval data suffices; plausibly this holds for depth-one or suitably 'tame' stratifications, which ties to Grothendieck's tame-topology programme.

deep.surprise_reason: The page consists of worked examples of a combinatorial device for stratified dévissage. The underlying idea is announced in Esquisse §5 and was later developed independently (Quinn, exit-path ∞-categories). The specific category Ĩ is a mildly interesting unpublished detail but is essentially a precursor sketch, and incomplete for higher depth.
transcription_corrections: In (22) the image shows V_{a,c} over V_{a,c}^* joined by a thick double-headed vertical arrow (not an explicit V_{a,c} ← V_{a,c}^*). In the same diagram V_{b,c} ← V_{b,c}^* is drawn as an upward arrow.
Top of page: a crossed-out line reads roughly 'V_{0,*} ← X_1^*'. The 'NB on ...' note is illegible, perhaps 'NB on n'aura...' or 'on mêmes'.
Under X_0^* in (20) there is a crossed-out downward arrow, consistent with the marginal variant diagram at top right, where X_0^* → V_{01} is drawn vertically.
The arrow V_{0,1}^* → X_1^* in (20) is downward, from V_{0,1}^* (not from V_{0,1}) to X_1^*; likewise for each row.
